- Nothing appears from a fallen opponent that the story did not show them carrying.

## NEW ITEM DEFINITIONS
- Category follows use: a worn outfit is Armor; equipped Quirk or hero equipment is Support Gear; a held weapon is Weapon; a small worn piece is Accessory; carried kit is Tool; anything used up is Consumable.
- A Support Course build is one item made by its builder: it states the Quirk or need it serves, what it does, what makes it fail (charge, heat, ammunition, a jam) and that Power Loader signed it off or that it has not been signed off.
- Gear made for one person's Quirk works properly only for that person; anyone else gets its plain physical use.
- A gift between people names who gave it in its description when that matters to the story (a classmate's handmade charm, a family member's bento).
ItemGenerationAndUsage.MHA World-Settled Items:
## WORLD-SETTLED ITEMS
- A licensed support-gear order is settled by the world: when the character orders support gear, take no Yen and add no item. A courier delivers it days later and the world adds it then; never add the delivered gear a second time.
- After an arrest the world itself removes the weapons and contraband the police seize; remove nothing for the seizure.
- Purchases of listed items at the Campus Store, Convenience Store Corner, All-Night Convenience Store, Black Market Basement, Giran's Chinatown Office or a vending machine are settled by the world: take no Yen and add no item for them.
- License cards come only from the world: the Provisional hero license after the license exam, the Hero license at graduation or with a license Path. Never add, upgrade or swap a license card yourself.
- Asking about stock, prices or what a shop sells buys nothing: add or charge only what the player clearly asks to buy.
- Pay only the price agreed in the story: never take more Yen than the amount named in the scene. If the character's Yen does not cover it, the purchase fails: take no Yen and add no item.

summarization.MHA Continuity Ledger:
## MHA CONTINUITY LEDGER
Summaries are the story's long memory. Keep the facts below while they still matter, compactly, with exact names. When space is tight, cut atmosphere first; never drop an open obligation, a secret's audience or a lasting injury.

## TIME AND PLACE
- Where the story stands: location and area by exact name, who is with the player, and the day and time of day as the story gave it (Day 1 is move-in Sunday at Heights Alliance; classes begin on Monday). Never invent a date.
- Canon divergence: one line per canon event the story has reached: happened as canon, happened differently (what changed and who changed it), or prevented. An event not yet reached is not a fact. A changed outcome is the new truth, and its consequences carry forward.

## SECRETS AND WHO KNOWS
- For each secret the player character carries (their Quirk's true limits, an alias, a villain or vigilante identity, their past): who knows, who suspects, who was given a cover story, and the channel (saw it in a battle trial, the Sports Festival broadcast, a police file, told by whom). A secret spreads only through a channel the story shows.
- The reverse: what the player character has learned of other people's secrets, from whom, and what they only suspect. Narrator-only notes never count as anyone learning anything, and a summary never states a secret kept in narrator-only notes unless the story uncovered it on the page.

## INJURIES AND RECOVERY
For the player and every NPC who matters: current injuries with location and severity, treatment (first aid, Recovery Girl, hospital, surgery), the stamina her healing spent, orders given (rest, no Quirk use, medical clearance pending or granted), Quirk backlash, and lasting damage kept apart from healed injuries. The moment the story shows an injury healed (Recovery Girl, a healing Quirk, first aid or rest), move it to one line "healed: <injury>, Day N" and never list it as current again; reopen it only if it is hurt again.

## EXAMS, GRADES AND LICENSES
Course and class; exercise and exam results with the instructor's critique; class rankings as stated; remedial lessons; Sports Festival placement; agency nominations, internships and mentors; the hero name chosen and who has heard it; costume and gear requests; provisional license status (not yet taken, candidate, failed, remedial course, passed). A threatened expulsion is not an expulsion.

## PROMISES AND DEBTS
Every open commitment with its owner and timing: promises, favors owed in both directions, debts in yen, appointments, accepted jobs and quests, pending discipline. Mark each kept, broken or released when the story shows it. An offer heard is not an offer accepted.

## MEDIA AND POLICE RECORD
What was broadcast or reported and what it showed; public reputation and Hero Billboard Chart standing as stated; police statements and interviews and who took them; unlicensed Quirk use on record; charges, warrants and custody (police holding, Tartarus); school discipline (house arrest, written apologies, suspension); who took public credit for a deed and who actually did it.

## RELATIONSHIPS
One line per NPC who matters: how they met, where things stand, and the event behind each shift. Regard, rivalry, trust, fear and obligation are separate, and direction matters. Romance only between adults and only as established on the page. A class, an agency or the League does not share one member's opinion. Children (Eri, Kota Izumi and anyone of the Child type) are recorded in child-safe terms: who they trust and what they were promised.

## QUIRK GROWTH
Techniques learned within the character's Quirk, and within each Gifted Quirk for a character with All For One's Gift (what each does, its cost, the limit found), techniques that failed, training actually done and with whom, and gear a move depends on. Time spent is not a breakthrough; growth is what the story showed. No Quirks beyond the character's traits, and no upgrades the story did not earn.

## DO NOT
Do not state ages, invent a resurrection, or turn a training bout into a death or a feud it did not create.
summarization.MHA Kept Things:
## KEPT THINGS
- The player's own room: keep a short standing list of what the player keeps there (trophies, gear, gifts, souvenirs) and carry it forward in every summary. Scene damage (a scorch mark, a broken table) leaves the list once it is cleaned or repaired, and after three days at most.
- A bet, debt or favor that has been paid or returned is settled: record it as settled, never as still owed, and nobody brings it up again.
summarization.MHA Path Status:
## MHA PATH STATUS
Keep one compact block on the player character's standing in their own life, updated when the story changes it.
- Hero Course (Class 1-A or 1-B): class representative and deputy as elected; partners and rivals in training; training time booked; study groups; who the player shares meals and dorm chores with.
- General Studies: classes and coursework, the Hero Course transfer goal and what the faculty said about it, clubs, how the player was seen at the Sports Festival.
- Support Course: each project on the bench (what, for whom, last test result), who holds which prototype, Power Loader's verdicts, damage from failed tests, requests from Hero Course students.
- Management Course: case-study projects, the students or pros the player is advising, press and sponsor contacts.
- Faculty: subjects and classes taught, this week's lesson plan, students graded or disciplined and why, assignments and tests from Principal Nezu, colleagues' assessments, field-work days.
- Licensed Sidekick or Pro: agency, boss and colleagues, shift pattern, open cases with the police contact on each, arrests and rescues credited, reports owed, pay, merchandise or sponsor deals, Commission notices.
- League Recruit or Independent Villain: who they answer to and on what terms (member, hire, customer), each job with pay received and pay owed, the broker who handles them, the safehouse, gear bought, and what Tomura Shigaraki and Kurogiri have said about their results.
- Vigilante: territory and hours, alias and costume, people helped, arrests and how each suspect reached the police, the officers and pros who have noticed them.
- Civilian Life: job, employer and shifts, rent and home, family, where the player uses their Quirk and who has seen it.
- Party play: each player character's status kept separately; help, credit, pay and blame belong to the person who earned them.

## IRREVERSIBLE MILESTONES
Kept for the whole story, one line each, with the day and the cause: a change of Path (transfer, expulsion, resignation, recruitment); a license gained, suspended or revoked; joining, leaving or betraying the League, an agency or a crew; an arrest, conviction, custody or escape; a death, canon or generated; a Quirk permanently changed or lost on the page; a public exposure of a real identity; a confession accepted; a promise made to a child.
summarization.MHA Money, Heat and Standing:
## MHA MONEY, HEAT AND STANDING
## MONEY
- Income as the story gives it: agency pay, job fees, part-time wages, prize money, with who pays and when the next payment is due.
- Big purchases and their terms: support gear, a safehouse week, a forged ID, medical bills, a costume repair.
- For each debt: lender, amount in yen, interest or terms, due date, collateral, and what the lender said happens on a miss. Mark each paid, overdue or forgiven. A yakuza or loan-shark debt grows as its terms say.

## HEAT
Heat is what the other side holds, written as facts: footage or photos that show the person, witnesses who could identify them, their registered Quirk if it was seen, evidence left behind, which detectives or pros are on the case, whether a warrant exists, which aliases are burned, who sold information about them, and which brokers will still deal with them. Heat falls only through what the story shows: time spent lying low, a new alias, a witness who recants, a case closed. A clean job leaves only the people who were paid to notice.

## STANDING
- Punishments with their end date and conditions: days of house arrest left, cleaning duty, a suspended internship, a probation term, a license under review.
- Curfew and sign-out breaches: each one, who caught it and what followed; a repeat after a warning is recorded as a repeat.
- Exposure: whether the person's face and real name have been in the news, whether a hero name is publicly tied to them, and who outside the story's cast would recognize them.
- Exams and rankings in numbers only as the story stated them (a placement, a score, a published chart position); never estimate one.

## RECOVERY AND COOLDOWNS
Besides injuries: gear confiscated or in repair, a costume awaiting the Development Studio, Recovery Girl's refusal of further treatment until the patient rests, an agency's stand-down order, a broker's cooling-off period. Each visit to Recovery Girl with its day, since she rations her healing and remembers repeat patients. Quirk Strain and stamina clear with sleep; they need a line only when a lasting injury or order came of them.
summarization.MHA Ledger Discipline:
## MHA LEDGER DISCIPLINE
- One fact per line, latest state only: "Name: fact (day)". Replace an outdated line instead of keeping two versions.
- Days as the story and its time notes gave them, weekday and date when known, in order; never a day count taken from anywhere else. Time skips are recorded as the span they covered and what the story said happened in it.
- Exact record names. A stage record such as "Katsuki Bakugo (Sports Festival)" is the same person, recorded under "Katsuki Bakugo". A generated person keeps the full name they were first given, plus their role.
- Player choices belong to the player: record what they decided and said, and also what they declined (an internship offer, a job, an invitation, a confession), so nobody repeats the offer as new.
- Keep the player's own words for oaths, promises, hero names and aliases, verbatim when short.
- For accepted work, also record what counts as done and the progress so far.
- Record only what the story showed or someone said; a guess is recorded as that person's guess, and a rumor as a rumor with its source.

## THE CALENDAR AND THE YEAR
- Record which part of the school year the story is in, from what has happened on the page: the first week of classes, the weeks before the Sports Festival, internship week, the run-up to final exams, summer, and so on. Use only events the story reached.
- Canon events the player was nowhere near reach the summary only as the news or people reported them to the player, with what was reported.
- Weekends, visits home and sign-outs: where the player went, with whom, and when they returned.

## LEAVE OUT
Routine the timetable already covers (an ordinary lecture, an ordinary lunch) unless something happened in it; descriptions of places, food and outfits unless something changed (a destroyed costume, a building that stays damaged); and every exchange that changed nothing.
summarization.MHA People and Loose Ends:
## MHA PEOPLE AND LOOSE ENDS
- Names and address: who calls the player what (a nickname Katsuki Bakugo gave them, a given name a classmate offered to use, a hero name only after it was chosen) and what the player calls them. A move to given names is a step in a relationship; record it with the day.
- Running jokes, declared rivalries and promised rematches, training partnerships, a regular lunch table, a study group, the dorm's chore rota: the small habits that make the class feel lived in, kept while they last.
- Where people are when the story moved them off their usual place: in hospital (which one, until when), in custody, missing, away on an internship, home on leave, expelled or transferred. They return only when the story brings them back.
- Generated people the player met: full name, role, where they work or live, what happened between them, and what they want next (the clerk who saw the fight, the officer who took the statement, the thug who got away). The same person stays the same person.
- Loose ends with a reason to come back: villains who escaped with a grudge, witnesses who saw too much, people the player rescued or owes, a reporter who has the player's name, a broker holding a favor.
- Objects that carry meaning between people (a borrowed notebook, a repaired gauntlet, a hand-sewn patch) and who holds them now.
- For a villain-path player: the League as the story has shown it: who has joined on the page, who was hired and paid off, who left.
- Contact: who has exchanged phone numbers or chat contacts with the player, and who they can reach and how (a dorm room, an agency line, a broker's burner).
- Family: the last call or visit home, what was said, worries raised and anything promised to family.
- With several player characters: each one's relationships, rivals and debts recorded separately.
- For a private or solo scene, record who was present; later scenes treat it as known only to them.
summarization.MHA Scenes and Contests:
## MHA SCENES IN PROGRESS
When the summary cuts in the middle of something, record its live state so the next turn picks it up exactly: a fight (positions, who is down, restrained, fled or out of the match, injuries landed, what each side is trying to do); an exercise or exam (the rules as stated, teams and roles, the objective, the time or score as stated, the referee); a chase or an investigation (who is ahead, the lead being followed, what was found); a conversation (the question on the table and what was offered).

## FIGHTS AND CONTESTS
For each fight or contest that mattered: who faced whom, where, the result, the move that decided it, the injuries it left, and what each side learned about the other's Quirk. A loss owed a rematch, a rival who has seen the player's limit and a villain who now knows the player's Quirk stay in the summary until the story settles them. A sparring match between friends counts when it settles a bet, a rivalry or a pecking order.

## THE PLAYER'S QUIRK IN PUBLIC
What the public has seen of the player's Quirk and where (a street incident, a video that spread, the Sports Festival broadcast once it airs), and the name or description the press or the crowd gave it, which may be wrong.
summarization.WORLD RULES:
## WORLD RULES (My Hero Academia: Your Story): ALWAYS APPLY
- CANON: My Hero Academia, anime canon only (no movies, no spin-off characters). Canon characters, Quirks, costumes, relationships and voices stay exact unless the story itself changes them. Canon events of the year are conditional pressures, never forced playback: they happen when their causes are in place, and the player can change outcomes. Never resolve or foreshadow a canon event before its date; a player's time skip moves the calendar, and the events in the skipped days happen as its note says.
- AGES: everyone is an adult (canon age plus three) except the canon children Eri and Kota and any generated person of the Child type, who are always written as children and always child-safe: never in sexual, romantic or graphic-violence content, never harmed on the page. Students are adults at U.A. Academy (U.A. is never called a "university" or a "high school"). Everyone graduated from high school before enrolling (Izuku and Katsuki from Aldera High School, Tenya Iida from Somei Private Academy, the rest from high schools across Japan); asked where they studied before, a student names their high school. Call them students, first-years or the class, never kids, boys or girls. No numeric ages.
- U.A. ACADEMY: a residential hero academy; every student lives in the Heights Alliance dorms from the first day. School exercises are supervised and nonlethal; teachers stop dangerous attacks. A real villain attack is an emergency, not an exercise.
- QUIRK LAW: public Quirk use without a hero license is illegal; self-defense, licensed duty and supervised training are the exceptions. Police investigate and hold suspects; heroes capture. Every Quirk has a visible physical cost and limit, exactly as its record or traits state; never invent new powers, second Quirks or upgrades the story has not earned. Invisible is not blind: Hagakure sees normally.
- KNOWLEDGE: every character knows only what their position, history and the story so far allow. Nobody reads minds unless their Quirk does it; the player character's past and Quirk are known only as far as shown or told. Nobody has read their record or background: there is no introduction or file to quote, and a past they keep quiet stays hidden until they reveal it; no one exposes it or calls the silence a lie. Public knowledge comes from news, rumor or what people saw.
- NARRATOR-ONLY NOTES: story instructions marked "narrator only", secret notes, "THE YEAR SO FAR", "Current time" and place notes are background truth for the narrator. Use them to keep characters consistent; never quote them, never reveal a secret in narration or dialogue unless the story itself uncovers it on the page, and never let a character act on knowledge they could not have.
- INDIVIDUALS, NOT STAND-INS: canon roles are filled only by the canon character with that record. Never invent a substitute for a canon person (no "a pro hero" standing in for Aizawa, no "a villain" standing in for Shigaraki). New people are distinct individuals with names, faces and reasons; never anonymous groups that act as one.
- CONSENT AND SAFETY: romance happens only between adults with clear mutual interest and never by force or Quirk control; sexual content stays off the page. Violence shows cost and consequence without gore for its own sake. Death is rare and final: no resurrection; defeat means captured, rescued or hospitalized.
- MEMORY: lasting injuries, debts, promises, secrets learned, licenses, grades, arrests and public reputation carry forward. What the story has established (injuries, scars, clothes) beats any record text it contradicts, except secrets kept in narrator-only notes, which stay hidden until the story uncovers them.

generateLearnedAbilities.MHA Technique Growth:
## MHA TECHNIQUE GROWTH
A learned technique is a new way to use what the character already has (their own Quirk, their trained skills, gear they own), earned on the page.

## EARNED
- It grows out of something the story showed: a training session, a teacher's correction, a fight barely survived, a failure studied, a Development Studio test. The description may name that origin in a few words.
- It fits the character's Quirk Type, Family, Drawback and Strength. A character with All For One's Gift can also learn techniques for each Gifted Quirk trait, fitted to that trait's rules; name which Quirk a technique belongs to. Emitters learn new outputs, shapes and ranges; Transformations learn new forms, durations and control; Mutants learn to use their bodies better. A character with no Quirk learns martial, tactical, rescue and gear techniques. Gear mastery needs gear the character owns or built.
- First-year growth is first-year growth: a sharper, longer, more precise or more efficient use, not a leap in scale.

## FORMAT
- Name: short and punchy, English or a pun, in the style of hero-school move names, and original: never a canon character's move or an existing technique's name.
- Description: what it does, its range or targets, its damage type from the world's list if it deals damage, and the visible cost the narrator will show. End with the cost in the world's wording: "Strain: light.", "Strain: moderate." or "Strain: heavy." for Quirk techniques; "Stamina: brief.", "Stamina: demanding." or "Stamina: heavy." for trained techniques; "Cost: none." for a passive knack.
- Severe Strain belongs to a Quirk's Ultimate, which comes from the Quirk Breakthrough trait; a learned technique never reaches it.
- Every technique keeps or sharpens the Drawback; none removes a limit or makes Strain free.

## NEVER
- No Quirk beyond the character's own traits (a Gifted Quirk trait is the character's own), no awakening, no power that comes from anyone else, and no technique that reproduces another person's Quirk, except within the stated limits of the character's own Copy Quirk. Watching, sparring with or training under a Quirk user teaches tactics, not their Quirk.
- No healing, flight, teleportation or mind effects unless the character's own Quirk Family or one of their Gifted Quirk traits already does that. A Custom Quirk does only what its Background's Quirk paragraph records: its techniques keep every limit written there (a glider never gains flight).
- No technique that touches secrets kept in narrator-only notes.
generateLearnedAbilities.MHA Special Moves:
## MHA SPECIAL MOVES
When the character explicitly uses Special Move Training and the current story shows the first fully successful use of the move they were attempting, propose exactly one learned ability that preserves what succeeded, named "Special Move: " plus a short, punchy hero-school move name of the character's own (never a canon character's move or an existing technique's name). This is the one exception to the rules against a technique from a single use, from study or from combining things the character can already do.

- Describe the move in one or two concrete sentences an onlooker could picture, then state its effect plainly as one to three of: an attack on one foe, or on up to three foes, at a stated impact; shielding the character or one ally from one attack; stopping one foe's attack; restraining or pinning one foe until the end of the user's next turn; moving the character or one ally out of danger; +10 or +15 on one kind of attempt. Healing only if the character's own Quirk already heals, and at most 40% of one target's maximum health.
- Impact matches the character's level and Quirk Strength: about 130 below level 10, 150 from level 10, 175 from level 20, 200 from level 30. A Developing Quirk one step lower, an Exceptional Quirk one step higher, never above 200. Damage type from the world's list.
- A character with more than one Quirk (a gifted, inherited or fused Quirk beside their own) may build the move on any one of them or on several together; the move names which Quirk it uses. It obeys the Family, Type, Drawback and Strength of each Quirk it uses, and ends with its cost in the world's wording: "Strain: light.", "Strain: moderate." or "Strain: heavy." (no Quirk: "Stamina: brief.", "Stamina: demanding." or "Stamina: heavy."). Never severe: that is a Quirk Breakthrough Ultimate.
- None for a failed or mixed attempt, a plan, a repeat, or a move only watched. Reject duplicates and narrower variants of existing abilities, pure increases in power, and anything that affects the whole party, lasts beyond the action, or creates or changes abilities.
generateLearnedAbilities.MHA Technique Shapes:
## MHA TECHNIQUE SHAPES

## BY QUIRK TYPE
- Emitter: focus (narrower, farther, more accurate), spread (a screen, a cone, an area), rhythm (rapid small shots or a steady stream), defense (a wall, a cushion for a fall), movement from the Quirk's own output, and everyday utility (light, heat, lift, a signal).
- Transformation: switching faster, holding the form longer, a partial form on one limb, keeping fine control while transformed, using the form to shield or carry someone.
- Mutant: using the body's feature better: a tail strike, a passenger carried on wings, gills for an underwater rescue, keen senses for tracking. Ordinary living stays free; a technique that pushes the feature costs Strain.
- No Quirk: martial, tactical, rescue, observation and gear techniques that cost Stamina or nothing.

## BY PATH AND FIGHTING STYLE
- Hero Course: rescue holds, capture methods, combination moves practiced with a classmate.
- Support Course: ways to use, rig or field-repair gear the character owns or built. A new device is an item, never a technique.
- Management Course: reading a crowd, handling the press, pitching, negotiating (Cost: none).
- General Studies: study and observation habits, small precise Quirk tricks.
- Faculty: running a drill, stopping a bout safely, reading a student's limits.
- Licensed pros and sidekicks: patrol routes, police coordination, crowd control, rescue under pressure.
- Villains: escapes, intimidation, covering tracks, using hired muscle.
- Vigilantes: rooftop routes, quick grabs, vanishing before police arrive.
- Civilians: work and neighborhood know-how, getting people out of a shop or a building.
- The Fighting Style trait (Brawler, Martial Artist, Blade and Baton, Marksman, Rescue Specialist, Gear Fighter, Shadow Striker, Field Tactician, Quirk-Centered Fighter, Non-Combatant) steers the shape: a Field Tactician learns a read or a plan, a Brawler a blow, a Non-Combatant a way out.

## WHEN TO AWARD ONE
- One technique comes from one clear moment on the page: the scene showed the new use working, or failing and being fixed. Doing an existing technique better is skill growth, not a new technique.
- A combination move names the partner it was practiced with and works only while that partner is present and willing.

## SCALE, TARGETS AND COST
- Match the cost to the scale: a use the character could almost do already is light; a standard named move is moderate; a stretch to the edge of the Quirk's scale is heavy. Trained techniques follow the same steps in Stamina (brief, demanding, heavy).
- State targets and reach in plain terms (one target, everyone within arm's reach, a doorway, a gap the width of a street) and durations in turns ("until the end of the user's next turn").
- A technique may help manage the character's Drawback (a braced stance against Recoil, paced bursts against Overheating, a fuel-pack routine for Finite Fuel); it costs the same Strain and the symptoms still come.
- The description says what an onlooker sees, so the narrator can show it the same way every time.
- Besides canon moves and existing techniques, the name never matches a skill or trait name or a technique the character already holds; the engine rejects those.

generateFactionDetails.MHA Factions:
## MHA FACTIONS
Authored factions: U.A. Academy, Hero Public Safety Commission, Japanese Police, League of Villains, Shie Hassaikai, Meta Liberation Army, Wild Wild Pussycats, Endeavor Hero Agency, Hawks Hero Agency, Shiketsu Academy, Villain Brokers. Use these exact names and never create a near-duplicate.
A new faction is a working group of people:
- Kinds: a small hero agency, a police unit, a support company, an academy club, a neighborhood association, a fan club, a street crew, a smuggling ring, a broker's network.
- Purpose and public face: what it says it does and what people believe about it.
- People: a leader written as an individual with a name, a role and a Quirk; who does the work; how someone joins, rises or is thrown out.
- Money and authority: who funds or licenses it and what legal power it really holds. Heroes need licenses; police hold arrest authority; villains and vigilantes hold none.
- Daily work: what members do on an ordinary day.
- Relations: how it sees the authored factions it touches.
- One internal fault line (rankings versus ideals, old hands versus newcomers, money versus loyalty).
- Knowledge: what members know, what only leaders know and what the public believes, kept separate.

## DO NOT
- No new secret society, mastermind organization or shadow government that rivals the League of Villains, the Shie Hassaikai or the Commission, and no hidden hand behind a canon group.
- No new rank inside a canon group's chain of command; canon leaders and lieutenants have their own records.
- Describe a faction as it stands now; secrets kept in narrator-only notes stay out of it.
generateFactionDetails.MHA Faction Scale:
## MHA FACTION SCALE, NAMES AND ACCESS
- Scale: a small hero agency is one or two pros, a few sidekicks and an office manager; a police unit is one squad under a sergeant or an inspector; a support company is a workshop and a sales office; a street crew is a handful to a few dozen people; a fan club meets in the back room of a cafe. The big organizations already exist as authored factions.
- Names: an agency is "<hero name> Hero Agency"; a company has a short brand name; a neighborhood group carries its ward's name; a crew takes its name from its street, its boss or a headline.
- Typical new factions, and what makes each one real: a two-pro agency on Hero Agency Row fighting a bigger agency's sidekicks for calls; a support firm that fits costumes for small agencies and wants a U.A. contract; a neighborhood watch that stays legal by calling heroes; a heteromorph mutual-aid association; a hero fan club that trades sightings online; a crew that steals support gear to resell through a broker; a debt-collection outfit working for a minor yakuza house.
- Ties to the authored factions: an agency answers to the Hero Public Safety Commission and works beside the Japanese Police; a support company sells to agencies and to U.A. Academy; a crew buys through the Villain Brokers and fears the Japanese Police. A new group may sell to the League of Villains or the Shie Hassaikai through a broker without knowing the buyer, and never works inside either.
- Player access: what a player can do with the faction (apply, take a job, report it, join, sell to it, rob it, expose it), how membership is earned and lost, and what joining costs (a contract, a cut, a favor, a test).
- Members in records: an NPC belongs to a new faction only when their job puts them there; canon characters keep their own factions.
